claims.statement: A femoral hernia passes beneath the inguinal ligament through the compartment medial to the femoral vein.
claims.limitation: Anatomical relationship, not diagnostic accuracy or a patient-specific probability.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: An indirect inguinal sac enters lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels at the deep ring; a direct defect protrudes medial to those vessels through the posterior inguinal wall.
claims.limitation: Cord fat distally does not by itself establish the proximal route.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: A stable reducible femoral hernia warrants timely elective repair assessment rather than applying the selected-male inguinal watchful-waiting policy.
claims.limitation: No exact deadline or universal operative method is asserted; evidence is largely observational.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Informed watchful waiting can be offered to selected men with an asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic reducible inguinal hernia.
claims.limitation: Does not extend to femoral hernias or establish that every groin pain is caused by the image; symptoms may later lead to surgery.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: A demonstrated inguinal hernia with concordant activity-limiting symptoms supports elective repair planning.
claims.limitation: Referral is not a promise to cure coexisting musculoskeletal pain or a ranking of all operations.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Coexisting hernia and musculoskeletal findings require symptom, site and activity correlation before assigning the functional limitation to the hernia.
claims.limitation: Case-specific reasoning from constructed observations; no validated symptom-attribution score or exclusive diagnosis is claimed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Clinical assessment with targeted ultrasound is appropriate when a suspected groin or recurrent hernia is not established on examination.
claims.limitation: Operator dependent; scanning the wrong location or not provoking an intermittent event does not establish absence at the symptomatic target.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Persisting diagnostic uncertainty after examination and ultrasound can justify dynamic MRI or CT; CT is an alternative when MRI is not possible.
claims.limitation: One directly verified guideline family; no universal MRI priority over hip assessment or diagnostic block, and no claim that MRI always resolves all pain sources.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: A posterior repair is recommended for a recurrent inguinal hernia after a prior anterior mesh repair.
claims.limitation: One directly verified guideline. Does not establish TEP superiority to TAPP; operative records, expertise and prior pelvic surgery matter.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: An anterior mesh repair is recommended for a recurrence after a prior posterior TEP or TAPP repair.
claims.limitation: One directly verified guideline; an incision described as open is not sufficient to identify the implanted mesh compartment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Recurrence after both anterior and posterior groin repairs warrants assessment by an expert hernia surgeon.
claims.limitation: Guideline family rather than independent corroboration; 2023 also records insufficient evidence for a universal technique after open preperitoneal repairs.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: In nonpregnant women, a preperitoneal laparo-endoscopic groin repair can detect and cover femoral as well as inguinal defects when expertise is available.
claims.limitation: Predominantly registry evidence and overlapping authors; not proof that every woman has a femoral defect.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Color Doppler can identify round-ligament varicosities mimicking a groin hernia during pregnancy; uncomplicated swelling can be observed.
claims.limitation: Small cohorts/case series; persistent severe pain, thrombosis or suspected visceral compromise requires reassessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Suspected strangulation in an acutely irreducible groin hernia supports emergency operative evaluation instead of manual reduction.
claims.limitation: Recommendations are strong despite low evidence; normal passage or an isolated normal biochemical result cannot resolve clinical ischemia concern.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Entrapment of part of a bowel wall can threaten that wall while the remaining lumen continues to permit intestinal passage.
claims.limitation: One verified case report/discussion reused offline from the harden1 ledger; supports the mechanism, not quantitative risk or comparative efficacy. Original source and clinical verification dates retained.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Reduced contrast enhancement of trapped bowel wall on CT is concerning for bowel compromise in an acute hernia.
claims.limitation: WSES discusses reduced CT wall enhancement as a predictor; it is not alone proof of irreversible necrosis. No sensitivity, specificity or numeric cutoff is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: A gentle manual reduction attempt can be considered for acute irreducibility when there is no suspicion of bowel ischemia; failed reduction requires emergency surgery.
claims.limitation: One current guideline, weak underlying evidence; hospital chart-review scenario, not authorization for forceful or unsupported office reduction.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: After successful manual reduction, observation continues until sedative or analgesic effects have resolved and the patient is clinically well.
claims.limitation: One guideline; no invented fixed observation duration or immediate-discharge rule. Persistent illness changes the pathway.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Diagnostic laparoscopy may assess bowel viability after a concerning acute groin hernia has reduced, including spontaneous reduction before inspection.
claims.limitation: Low-certainty conditional approach, not mandatory laparoscopy for every recovered patient.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Bowel resection without gross enteric spillage does not automatically exclude a permanent macroporous synthetic mesh groin repair.
claims.limitation: HerniaSurge 2023 is a weak recommendation. Mesh is a permissible option, not a compulsory operation in every case; evidence overlaps WSES.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: For a stable patient with gross enteric contamination and a small groin defect suitable for closure, primary tissue repair is supported.
claims.limitation: One older guideline, grade 2C; its small-defect recommendation uses less than 3 cm. No broad rule for large contaminated ventral defects or biologic mesh superiority.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Diagnostic nerve blocks may contribute to chronic postoperative groin-pain evaluation but transient relief is not a unique proof of cause or a guarantee of surgical benefit.
claims.limitation: One current guideline, very-low/low evidence. No universal response threshold or single-block surgery-selection rule.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Failure to improve after one chronic groin-pain block does not by itself establish recurrence or exclude a neuropathic contribution.
claims.limitation: One guideline; injection targeting, overlap and multiple pain mechanisms limit interpretation. No automatic escalation to mesh removal.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Chronic postrepair groin pain can include neuropathic and nonneuropathic components, so new mechanical findings require renewed anatomical assessment.
claims.limitation: Phenotypic assessment is not proof of one injured named nerve. Recurrence and non-hernia sources must be considered.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Persistent complex postoperative inguinal pain is best assessed through a specialist multidisciplinary hernia/pain service before invasive treatment selection.
claims.limitation: Single directly verified guideline; does not choose selective versus triple neurectomy or mesh removal for every patient.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: HerniaSurge suggests at least three months of pharmacologic/interventional treatment and at least six months after repair before proceeding to more invasive CPIP treatment.
claims.limitation: Weak recommendation, not a universal guarantee that surgery becomes indicated when these intervals elapse.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Evidence for pain surgery is limited, and neurectomy or mesh removal can fail or worsen pain.
claims.limitation: Single current guideline; no new exact response probability, universal operation or cure promise is used.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Local anesthesia is supported for open repair of a reducible inguinal hernia by experienced teams and can benefit frail patients.
claims.limitation: Strong general local-anesthesia recommendation; frail-patient comparative evidence is weaker. Exact anesthetic drugs or doses are outside scope.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Prior pelvic or prostatic surgery and the need for local anesthesia can favor an anterior open approach over routine laparo-endoscopic repair.
claims.limitation: Not an absolute contraindication to expert laparoscopy and not a universal superiority claim.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: An incidental asymptomatic contralateral defect does not by itself justify automatic repair; possible intervention should be addressed during consent.
claims.limitation: Evidence is weak; distinguish an occult opposite-side finding from a symptomatic bilateral hernia and respect the actual consent.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Mesh repair is recommended for most adults; an expert Shouldice repair remains a supported selected non-mesh option after informed choice.
claims.limitation: Does not establish all-patient equivalence of tissue and mesh operations or rank a surgeon without the relevant expertise.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: For laparo-endoscopic repair of a large direct defect, heavier mesh is supported to reduce recurrence; light mesh has not demonstrated a chronic-pain advantage in that setting.
claims.limitation: Recommendation is technique- and defect-dependent. Do not transfer the preference to open Lichtenstein repair; weight thresholds vary across studies.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Postrepair pain reproduced within the testicle requires assessment of scrotal-content and urological causes rather than being presumed to arise from cutaneous scrotal innervation.
claims.limitation: One directly verified current guideline, Chapter 19; not a substitute for urgent assessment of sudden severe scrotal pain.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the represented groin-repair or postrepair-pain scenario.

claims.statement: HerniaSurge suggests general or local rather than regional anesthesia in older adults, with urinary-retention and medical-complication concerns contributing to individual selection.
claims.limitation: One guideline; the recommendation for age 65 and older is weak. No individualized adverse-event probability or universal contraindication is claimed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the represented groin-repair or postrepair-pain scenario.

claims.statement: Lightweight mesh is recommended in open Lichtenstein repair to reduce chronic pain and foreign-body sensation.
claims.limitation: One current guideline; this preference must not be transferred unchanged to laparo-endoscopic repair.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the represented groin-repair or postrepair-pain scenario.

claims.statement: A documented superficial sensory response can help separate a skin-provoked symptom from pain still reproduced by deeper scrotal-contents examination.
claims.limitation: Original application of guideline skin/content differentiation and diagnostic-block limitations, not a validated localization test. One directly verified guideline family; the observation neither proves a specific cause nor excludes neural overlap.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed groin-repair or postrepair-pain scenario; not a universal diagnostic or operative ranking.

claims.statement: Contrast-enhanced CT can contribute to assessment of suspected bowel compromise when the clinical assessment of an acute groin episode is uncertain.
claims.limitation: WSES addresses predictors of strangulation with low-quality evidence; it does not mandate CT before every reduction attempt or verify a universal timing threshold. The exact taxis-versus-CT ranking remains a clinician-review application of this and reduction-selection claims.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed groin-repair or postrepair-pain scenario; not a universal diagnostic or operative ranking.

claims.statement: Controlled bowel resection without gross enteric spillage represents a clean-contaminated field rather than a clean procedure.
claims.limitation: The operative-field classification is distinct from the weak and context-dependent evidence for a particular repair material. No infection probability or mandatory mesh operation is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed groin-repair or postrepair-pain scenario; not a universal diagnostic or operative ranking.

claims.statement: Prior prostatic or pelvic surgery is a reason to individualize the usual primary laparo-endoscopic repair preference and can favor an anterior open approach.
claims.limitation: One directly verified current guideline family; this is a relative planning consideration, not an absolute prohibition on expert TEP/TAPP. Combine separately with the experienced-team local-open claim for the exact cooperative patient; no universal postoperative technique ranking is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed groin-repair or postrepair-pain scenario; not a universal diagnostic or operative ranking.

exactRetainedClaim.statement: A stable reducible femoral hernia warrants timely elective surgical repair planning even when symptoms are mild or absent.
exactRetainedClaim.limitation: Pain, irreducibility, obstruction, or ischemic concern changes the pathway to emergency assessment; the evidence base is largely observational.
exactRetainedClaim.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a confirmed reducible femoral hernia and no emergency feature.

exactRetainedClaim.statement: An indirect inguinal hernia enters the inguinal canal through the deep ring lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels.
exactRetainedClaim.limitation: The vessel relationship classifies anatomy but does not establish acuity or select a repair technique.
exactRetainedClaim.applicablePopulation: Adults whose operative or imaging report directly describes a groin hernia's relationship to the inferior epigastric vessels.

exactRetainedClaim.statement: Watchful waiting is a safe option for informed men with asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic reducible inguinal hernias, although later repair is common when symptoms develop.
exactRetainedClaim.limitation: This does not apply to women, femoral hernias, activity-limiting symptoms, irreducibility, obstruction, or strangulation.
exactRetainedClaim.applicablePopulation: Men with a confirmed reducible inguinal hernia and absent or minimal symptoms.

exactRetainedClaim.statement: The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve supplies the anterolateral and lateral thigh, so isolated sensory symptoms there after inguinal surgery are compatible with irritation of this nerve.
exactRetainedClaim.limitation: The pattern is compatible rather than diagnostic; weakness, progression, or a broader distribution requires evaluation for another lesion.
exactRetainedClaim.applicablePopulation: Adults with isolated anterolateral-thigh sensory symptoms and preserved strength after laparoscopic inguinal repair.

exactRetainedClaim.statement: Persistent pain, irreducibility, obstruction or ischemic concern would change the stable femoral-herniation scenario to urgent assessment; the described reducing, nontender finding without obstructive symptoms does not establish that emergency.
exactRetainedClaim.limitation: Case-bound acuity distinction from the recorded claim limitation, not a rule that absence of a single symptom excludes incarceration or ischemia.
exactRetainedClaim.applicablePopulation: Only the identified constructed flags3 clinic/audit scenarios; no general test-performance, risk, timing or treatment cutoff is introduced.
